title: Checkpoint: Sparta and War
objective: After this level you can explain how the Greeks beat Persia and then fought each other.
summary: Sparta and Athens fought Persia side by side, as the Serpent Column still records, then turned their leagues on each other; Persia, beaten at sea, helped decide the Greek war.

cards.headline: Chapter 4 finale: one monument lists Sparta and Athens side by side.
cards.body: It celebrated beating Persia together. By 431 BCE, the two names at the top were at war.

cards.headline: A victory monument, with an argument built in
cards.body: After Plataea, 31 Greek cities dedicated a gold tripod at Delphi on a bronze column of three twisted snakes. The Spartan commander Pausanias first had it inscribed in his own name; the allies objected, and the cities’ names replaced it, with Sparta first, then Athens and Corinth. Constantine later moved the column to Constantinople. It still stands in Istanbul, minus its snake heads.

questions.prompt: Sparta and War recap: who were the helots?

options.label: Serfs owned by the Spartan state
Sparta’s elected officials
Persian soldiers captured at Marathon
Athenian rowers in the fleet

questions.explanation: Helots were serfs owned by the Spartan state who farmed the land and handed over half their produce.

questions.prompt: Sparta and War recap: whose tactics won at Marathon, and how?

options.label: Leonidas, holding a narrow pass
Themistocles, luring ships into a strait
Miltiades, with strong wings and a thin center
Lysander, with Persian gold

questions.explanation: Miltiades strengthened his wings and left his center thin, and the wings surrounded the Persians.

questions.prompt: Why was the first inscription on the Serpent Column replaced?

options.label: It praised the Persians
Pausanias named himself, and the allies objected
It was written in Persian
options.rationale: The problem was whose name it bore.

options.label: Athens wanted its name first

questions.explanation: The Spartan commander Pausanias had it inscribed in his own name; the allies objected, and the cities’ names replaced it.

questions.prompt: Sparta and War recap: how did Athens and Sparta differ as military powers?

options.label: Athens ruled the sea; Sparta’s strength was on land
Sparta ruled the sea; Athens’s strength was on land
options.rationale: It was the other way round.

options.label: Both relied on Persian armies
options.rationale: They fought Persia, then each other.

options.label: Neither had a navy or an army

questions.explanation: Athens built its power on triremes and the Delian League; Sparta on helot-fed citizen soldiers and the strongest army on land.

questions.prompt: Sparta and War recap: which order of events is right?

options.label: Delian League founded, Plataea, Peloponnesian War
Plataea, Delian League founded, Peloponnesian War
Peloponnesian War, Plataea, Delian League founded
Plataea, Peloponnesian War, Delian League founded
options.rationale: The league came before the war.

questions.explanation: Plataea ended the invasion in 479 BCE, the Delian League formed in 478 BCE, and the Peloponnesian War ran from 431 to 404 BCE.
